HIIT pushes your aerobic engine, helping you get fitter, recover faster and feel less gassed in hard fast efforts. 4.	Improve endurance and work capacity.   The repeated intervals teach your body to handle intensity better.  Over time consistency builds and you can play with the variables of recovery.  The benefits carries over to other sport, training and everyday energy. 5.	Time-efficient and low-impact. not all hair care has to break you bank💰 1. brush starting at your ends and work your way up -starting at your ends helps remove tangles little by little instead of pulling one big knot through your entire strand. this puts a lot less tension on your hair, helps prevent unnecessary breakage, and is especially important if your hair is fine or prone to tangling. 2. scalp massages -i like to do a 5 to 10 minute scalp massage every day. this can help increase blood flow to the scalp, helps distribute your natural oils, and feels amazing. i personally do it because it’s great for overall scalp health and can support healthier, denser hair over time.  3. never sleep with wet hair -wet hair is at its weakest, so tossing and turning on a pillow all night creates extra friction that can lead to breakage, frizz, and split ends. it may seem convenient but in the long run it causes so much damage.  4. always split and rinse your hair after shampoo and conditioner -don’t just let the water run over the top of your head. separate your hair into sections and make sure you’re rinsing all the way down to your scalp and underneath your hair. leftover shampoo or conditioner can cause buildup, weigh your hair down, and even contribute to an itchy or irritated scalp. 5. wear protective hairstyles -protective styles help reduce friction, tangles, and unnecessary breakage throughout the day. i usually wear a very loose claw clip updo or a loose french braid. the key is keeping them loose, not tight. if your hairstyle is pulling on your scalp, it’s too tight. healthy hair isn’t about finding one miracle product. it’s all the little habits you stay consistent with that make the biggest difference over time💪🏻    #hair #haircare #healthyhair  #hairtips #kayliboyle

top 5 tips to start your healthy hair care journey🌱✨ 1. cut off those split ends✂️      split ends can’t be repaired, only temporarily sealed. if you leave them, they can continue splitting farther up the hair shaft, leading to more breakage over time. regular trims help keep your hair looking thicker and healthier while preventing you from losing more length later. 2. do a 10 minute scalp massage daily💆🏼‍♀️      your scalp is skin, and healthy hair starts there. daily scalp massages can help increase blood flow to the scalp, reduce buildup, and create a healthier environment for your hair to grow. you can use your fingertips or a scalp massager. just be gentle and consistent. 3. start scalp + hair oiling🫶      find the right hair oil for your scalp and hair type because not every oil works for everyone. i oil my scalp for density, not to make my hair grow faster. massage it in for a few minutes 1 to 3 times a week before wash day, then wash it out after 3 to 4 hours if your scalp tolerates it well. i also have other videos that go into all the do’s and don’ts of hair oiling if you want to learn more. 4. get a blood panel done🩸      if your hair feels thinner than normal, sheds excessively, or isn’t growing like it used to, it may be worth asking your doctor for blood work. things like low iron, vitamin d, b12, zinc, or other deficiencies can affect hair health. if you’re deficient, focus on vitamin rich foods and only take supplements if recommended by your healthcare provider. 5. learn your hair before buying products🤍      figure out your hair pattern (straight, wavy, curly, or coily), strand texture (fine, medium, or coarse), porosity (how well your hair absorbs and holds moisture), and scalp type (oily, dry, balanced, or sensitive). once you know those, it’s much easier to build a routine that actually works for you instead of wasting money on products that aren’t a good fit. healthy hair isn’t about buying the most expensive products. it’s about understanding your hair, staying consistent, and being patient. 🤍   #haircare #healthyhair #HairCareTips #kayliboyle

Ocean to table - 🦀 Ganjang Gejang (Soy Marinade Raw Crab) Recipe  - Crab - Vegetable (garlic, ginger, onion, green onion, chili) - Korean Ganjang (from @kisoondo) Q. what is Korean ganjang? Korean ganjang (Hansik-ganjang) is a 100% naturally fermented soy sauce made only from meju, salt, and water over several months or years. In contrast, acid-hydrolyzed soy sauce is a chemically produced alternative where hydrochloric acid breaks down defatted soybeans in just a few days. The traditional Korean ganjang delivers a clean, sharp saltiness with deep umami from natural fermentation :) Q. Why should we use frozen crab for Ganjang Gejang? Crab must be flash-frozen for ganjang-gejang to ensure both food safety and the perfect texture. Once caught, crabs immediately activate natural proteolytic enzymes that dissolve their own muscle tissue, but flash-freezing at ultra-low temperatures instantly halts this self-digestion, preventing the meat from turning mushy. Furthermore, because this dish is cured raw rather than cooked, this freezing process is critical to eliminate dangerous marine bacteria and parasites like lung flukes lurking in the crab's shell and gills. #koreanfood
